input.question: - why does 3G feel like 1G or like it doesn't work all when a few years back it seemed like high speed beauty?
input.ground_truth: Part of it is that you're used to the LTE speed, so when you're running on 3G things just seem slow. On top of that, as faster connections become more common mobile websites are getting more complicated. This does mean that some pages will take longer to load on 3G now than they used to, but that's because the pages have changed. Of course the connection could be the issue. If the network in that particular area is very congested and/or you have low signal strength, then those will impact your speeds. Both of those problems are more common in areas where there's relatively little coverage; areas with a high degree of coverage usually have LTE available.

Question: - why does 3G feel like 1G or like it doesn't work all when a few years back it seemed like high speed beauty?

A long time ago, we had a small road called "2G." It was slow, like a road where cars could only go a little bit at a time.

Then, we got a bigger and faster road called "3G." At first, it felt super fast, like a big highway where lots of cars could zoom quickly! That’s why it felt like "high speed beauty."

But now, we have even bigger and faster roads called "4G" and "5G." So, the old "3G" road feels much slower, almost like the old small road (1G). That’s why 3G now feels slow or like it doesn’t work well—it’s because we have even faster roads now, and 3G just can’t keep up!
